key_insight: LizTail combines shape adaptation and spatial parallelism in one systolic-array design by reconfiguring a 128×128 array into 32 segment-level units with only predefined connections, avoiding full fine-grained routing.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for accelerating both CNN inference and LLM decoding, especially when workload shape and available parallelism vary widely and fixed arrays waste many PEs.
method: Partitions the array into 32 regular 128×4 segments
Supports trimming, 180° turn-back extension, and distributed execution across subarrays
Uses differentiated PE datapaths plus segment-aware CEB/SIB buffers, guided by a hardware-constrained mapper
evidence_signal: The abstract reports geometric-mean speedups of 5.02× on CNN inference and 25.67× on LLM decoding over a TPU-like array, with EDP reduced by up to 38.23×.
watch_item: The design may add hardware and mapping complexity because flexibility is achieved through segment-level constraints, specialized buffers, and a constrained execution mapper.
paper_title: LizTail: Unifying Shape Adaptation and Spatial Parallelism with Segment-Reconfigurable Systolic Arrays
